correctness.rationale: A complete incidence-row bijection modulo plant permutations enumerates every connected graph with each \(a+b\le8\). Each survivor-set component order is separately computed by disjoint-set union and breadth-first flood fill, with equality asserted for every case. All 55 comparisons of unequal coefficient vectors within equal degree-signature classes are coordinatewise ordered, proving no crossover because the expectation is a nonnegative-basis polynomial. At nine vertices, the exact coefficient vectors differ by (0,0,-1,1,2,0), yielding \(q(1-q)^2(2-3q)\), whose only interior root is 2/3 and whose sign changes. Independent exact subset matching confirms equality for all 32 survivor sets. The included Python standard-library checker was run successfully; no continuous/infinite claim relies on partial enumeration.

originality.rationale: The closest fully examined original work, Solé and Montoya 2000, measures largest ecological clusters under random removal but reports simulations of three large food webs, not exact coefficientwise dominance up to eight species or an explicit nine-species crossover with identical matching response. Dunne et al. 2002 concern secondary extinctions and connectance. Kitsak et al. 2017 study stability under bond rather than one-guild site percolation. Chabert-Liddell et al. 2021/2022 give stochastic-block-model predictions of sequential ecological robustness rather than the exact functional, according to available abstracts; inaccessible full text and supplements remain a bibliographic risk, not represented as checked. Indexed research and relevant exact-graph queries did not identify a covering result. The witness retains matching equality on every survivor subset, so known matching-capacity reversals cannot imply this result.
residual_risks: Full text and supplementary material for Chabert-Liddell et al. were unavailable; a covered exact special case could have been overlooked.
Other reliability-theory or ecological-network literature could describe the equivalent graph polynomial under an alternative name.
No independent audit or external novelty certification has been performed.

value.rationale: The largest surviving connected component directly measures potential fragmentation of a species interaction network. Sharp minimal-order and coefficientwise classification control for guild sizes and both degree multisets. The nine-vertex example shows a risk-ranking reversal as failure pressure changes; yet maximum one-to-one matching capacity agrees for every failure subset, proving the effect reflects connectivity organization and not even a change in instantaneous assignment capacity. This is a natural structural boundary for a standard robustness functional rather than an arbitrary subgraph slice. It is not a statement about actual persistence under ecological dynamics.
